subtype: Grieving and sorrowful away from home [Regulating]
passage: Sunday night, 11 pm. Papa called this morning to say Nani had died in her sleep. I'm in Pune. The funeral was today, and I couldn't get a train in time. I said I was fine on the phone. I said it twice. Then I went to my room and looked at her photo on my shelf for an hour. I'm Neelam, and this is the first time I've written a diary in months. My roommate Swati came in with tea and didn't ask anything. She sat on the floor. I told her about Nani's mango pickle and started to cry. I lit a small lamp by the photo. Tomorrow I'll call Papa again and ask him about her last days. I think I want to ask the college counsellor too.

qa.q: Why did Neelam tell Papa that all was fine, and what did Neelam do instead after the call?
qa.a: Neelam likely wanted to stay composed far from home, but afterward looked at Nani's photo, cried with Swati and lit a small lamp.

qa.q: What could Neelam do next for self-support while away from family?
qa.a: Neelam can call Papa again, keep marking the loss with the lamp, and talk to the college counsellor.

qa.q: How might Swati's quiet presence have helped Neelam?
qa.a: Swati did not ask questions and just sat with Neelam, so Neelam could speak about Nani when ready.

grounding: Neelam grieves far from home, puts on a brave face, then reaches out, marks the loss and thinks of a counsellor.

subtype: Grieving and sorrowful away from home [Regulating]
passage:
Shankar: hey, are you up
Madhav: yeah. couldn't sleep
Shankar: I heard about your uncle. I'm really sorry
Madhav: thanks. I keep saying I'm okay to everyone at home
Shankar: are you
Madhav: not really. I'm four hours away and I couldn't go for the rites
Shankar: that's hard. do you want to talk about him?
Madhav: he taught me to ride a bicycle in the fields
Shankar: tell me more if you want
Madhav: maybe tomorrow. can we sit together at lunch
Shankar: of course. and if it keeps feeling heavy, the counsellor at college is kind. I can walk you over
Madhav: ok. thank you for staying up

qa.q: How far away from home was Madhav?
What is Madhav feeling under his "I'm okay", and how does Madhav show it?
qa.a: Madhav feels sad and cut off from his family, shown by admitting he is not really okay and had missed the rites.

qa.q: What could Madhav do to keep taking care through this?
qa.a: Madhav could keep talking to Shankar, mark the uncle's memory in a personal way, and visit the college counsellor if the heaviness continues.

qa.q: How might Shankar feel about staying up with Madhav?
qa.a: Shankar seems caring and concerned, and Shankar offered to listen and walk with Madhav to the counsellor.

grounding: Madhav grieves away from home and moves from saying all is fine to reaching out to a friend.
